summary.headline: Natco Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR816.9 crores (from INR1,287.3 crores) on Revlimid decline; FY27 PAT guided at INR700-750 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated net revenue was INR816.9 crores versus INR1,287.3 crores a year earlier, and profit was INR269 crores including associate share, versus INR406 crores, with a one-time INR115 crore tax benefit from the new tax regime in the period. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR4,375.9 crores (INR4,784 crores in FY25) and net profit INR1,418.5 crores (INR1,883.4 crores). Management said the decline reflects the absence of lenalidomide (Revlimid) and guided FY27 as a base year with revenue of INR3,400-3,500 crores and PAT of INR700-750 crores, including the South African associate. Management framed FY28 onward as a 15-25% compounding phase driven by exclusivities, Brazil and Canada launches.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (Brazil, Canada, others)
segments.commentary: FY26 subsidiary sales were about INR730 crores. Brazil sub sales were about INR257-280 crores (including INR30 crores direct billing from India) and are expected to rise to INR550-600 crores in FY27. Canada FY26 sales were INR229 crores, guided to grow 10-15%.

segments.name: Associate: Adcock Ingram (South Africa, ~35% stake)
segments.commentary: Management expects Adcock revenue of $580-600 million and PAT of $47-48 million in FY27, subject to exchange rate and war-related factors. Associate profit is included in the INR700-750 crore PAT guidance.

segments.name: Crop Health Sciences (agrochemicals)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales close to INR140 crores versus about INR60 crores last year, per management. Business is predominantly domestic and being demerged from the company.

segments.name: Semaglutide (India)
segments.commentary: Vial launched on day one and is the only generic vial in the market; pen launched about a month later in April. Brand run-rate is about INR2 crores a month, with partners Eris and Glenmark taking the combined bump to about INR4-5 crores a month; target INR75-100 crores annualised.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR3,400-3,500 crores and PAT at INR700-750 crores, with some buffer for West Asia war impacts.
South African associate FY27 revenue of $580-600 million and PAT of $47-48 million, dependent on exchange rate.
FY27 is a base year with no major exclusivity launches; management guided to 15-25% earnings compounding every year from FY28.
Effective tax rate from FY27-28 expected around 25% including surcharge.
R&D spend expected at 7-9% of revenue next year, already budgeted in PAT.
Brazil sub revenue guided to INR550-600 crores this year; Canada growth 10-15% in FY27.
Expects 1-2 first-to-file or complex US filings this year out of 8-9 planned filings; Vizag US FDA inspection expected anytime this year.
Targets a 70:30 split of profit between base business and first-to-file/special products over the next 5 years, versus the reverse historically.
capex_capacity: Four US FDA-approved facilities: 2 API plants (Chennai, Mekaguda) and 2 finished dosage plants (Kothur, Vizag). Kothur, Chennai and Mekaguda were inspected in 2025 and cleared with EIRs; Vizag has not been inspected for a long time and inspection is expected this year.
Demerger of the Crop Health Sciences business is in progress.
US front-end business still loss-making; management hopes to break even this year. Indonesia also still loss-making.
demand_pricing: Lenalidomide (Revlimid) decline drove the YoY sales fall; management said FY27 has practically no lenalidomide contribution.
Pomalidomide first-wave launch was highly competitive with 4-5 generics sharing exclusivity; no meaningful Q4 bump.
Semaglutide India: pen market priced around INR3,000-4,000 a month versus under INR1,000 for the vial; management says vial is capturing price-sensitive demand.
West Asia war: supply to Middle East maintained with higher freight from rerouting. Agrochem raw material costs up 25-30%; pharma has inventory cover, so impact expected later in the year.
Management said US generic competition is intense, with 7-20 filers on NCE-1 products, making first-to-file opportunities rare.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 sales decline only Revlimid, and was there any West Asia war impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the decline is mainly Revlimid. Middle East supply was maintained despite some challenges, but freight costs rose due to rerouting from traditional carriers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise as a share of sales in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher R&D expense plus an engineering and spares inventory write-down; R&D and write-down together were about INR20-30 crores, with R&D the larger part.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue INR3,400-3,500 crores and PAT INR700-750 crores, including the associate profit and a buffer for war-related factors.

qa_highlights.question: What drives growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some US exclusivities in FY27-28, plus Brazil and Canada launches with approvals expected in H2 FY27; earnings are guided to compound 15-25% a year from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of M&A and the buyback question?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working on a couple of transactions with net cash of about INR2,400 crores and hopes to close one in FY27; it declined to consider a buyback and said valuations outside India are more reasonable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the agrochem exposure to the West Asia war?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs are up 25-30%, but about half of kharif procurement is done. Agrochem is mainly domestic and more exposed than pharma exports; impact expected later in the year.

risks_watch: FY27 is a base year with no major exclusivity launches; PAT falls to about half of FY26 level.
Semaglutide competition in India is intense; pen and vial revenue run-rates are still small.
West Asia war raises freight and raw material costs; agrochem domestic margins at risk later in FY27.
Pending Vizag US FDA inspection this year.
Large cash pile (about INR2,400 crores) earmarked for acquisitions, with no target disclosed and no buyback planned.
Associate earnings are exposed to the rand/dollar exchange rate and NATCO holds only about 35% of Adcock Ingram.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term diversification and pipeline, but candid that FY26-27 earnings will decline sharply. Management was evasive on specific exclusivities, product names, acquisition targets and timelines, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: I think we have always guided there will be a decline.
So '27 will be a base year where we'll settle around INR700 crores, INR750 crores.
So I'm personally very excited. But these are all like moon shots, as you know.
